result_semantic_payload.summary: The hypothesis that employee lihua exported the customer database on 2024-05-10 is NOT supported by the recorded evidence. The export was performed by the automated nightly scheduled job `nightly_export`, running under the dedicated non-interactive service account `svc_export`, not by lihua. The application log /export/app.log records the job trigger at 2024-05-09 23:55:01 (account=svc_export) and the export completing at 2024-05-10 01:03:40 with status=success, duration=18s, exporting 184,112 customer rows to /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz. The scheduler definition /scheduler/jobs.conf independently corroborates this: job nightly_export runs daily at 23:55, run_as svc_export, task export_customers. The README confirms svc_export is a dedicated non-interactive service account used by scheduled jobs. The only recorded lihua activity is two FAILED login attempts from 198.51.100.44 at 2024-05-10 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 (reason=password) — occurring ~44 minutes AFTER the export completed and both unsuccessful, so lihua had no authenticated session during the export window. Note: the delegated profile was 'windows', but the actual image contains a Linux-style seized application server (scheduler + export log); no Windows registry, prefetch/amcache, or event-log evidence exists in this scope.

claim_candidates.text: The customer database export on 2024-05-10 was executed by the automated scheduled job 'nightly_export' under the service account 'svc_export', not by employee lihua. The hypothesis is refuted.
limitations: Single application log is the sole execution record; no independent OS-level audit trail (e.g. syslog, cron log, auth.log) was present in the scope to corroborate.

claim_candidates.text: The export completed successfully at 2024-05-10 01:03:40 (duration 18s), exporting 184,112 rows of dataset 'customers' to /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz, following a scheduler trigger at 2024-05-09 23:55:01.

The job's schedule (daily 23:55, run_as svc_export, task export_customers) in /scheduler/jobs.conf is consistent with the observed trigger time 23:55:01, indicating a routine scheduled export rather than a manual or ad-hoc action.
limitations: jobs.conf carries no integrity hash or modification history, so the definition cannot be proven unaltered; mtime/ctime for all files are identical (1790594134), which is an artifact of image packaging rather than real file timestamps.

claim_candidates.text: lihua's only recorded activity is two failed login attempts from 198.51.100.44 at 2024-05-10 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 (reason=password), occurring approximately 44 minutes after the export completed; lihua therefore had no authenticated session during the export window.

The failed logins from a single external IP immediately after the export are consistent with a password-guessing or credential-testing attempt and warrant separate review, but they do not establish lihua as the exporter.
limitations: Two attempts alone is a thin basis; no account lockout, MFA, or geolocation evidence is available. The IP 198.51.100.44 is in the TEST-NET-2 documentation range, suggesting sanitized/test data.

Profile/scope mismatch: the delegation specified platform 'windows', but the image contains a Linux-style seized application server (scheduler config + application export log). No Windows artifacts exist — no registry, no prefetch/amcache, no Security/Sysmon event logs — so the Windows execution-corroboration rule could not be applied.
Only 3 files are present in the scope (440/206/116 bytes); there is no OS audit trail to independently corroborate the single application log.
Filesystem timestamps are uniform across all files (1790594134), an image-packaging artifact, so they provide no real time ordering.
The exported artifact /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz is referenced in the log but is not present in the scope, so export integrity and downstream transfer are unverified.
jobs.conf has no integrity hash or change history, so it cannot be proven unaltered.
The source IP 198.51.100.44 falls in the TEST-NET-2 documentation range (198.51.100.0/24), suggesting sanitized or synthetic data; real-world geolocation/ownership analysis is not possible.
warnings: Hypothesis refuted: the recorded evidence attributes the export to the automated service account svc_export, not to employee lihua.
The uniform timestamps (1790594134) across all files and the identical cluster key for all three CREATED events indicate a synthetic/packaged image; treat file-level timestamps as non-forensic.
Platform scope mismatch: investigation was conducted against the actual Linux-style content rather than the declared 'windows' profile.
